guards.what: N1: `CreatureCmd.Damage(ctx, Owner.Creature, DamageVar(16m, ValueProp.Unpowered), null, null)` (PrecariousShears.cs:30) vs `run.lose_hp(16)` (precarious_shears.py:20)
guards.rationale: Two differences, neither observable. (a) FLAGS: the C# DamageVar is Unpowered but NOT Unblockable (PrecariousShears.cs:21), while RunState.lose_hp's docstring describes itself as `Unblockable | Unpowered` (run.py:294-298). Out of combat the player has no Block -- Block is a CombatState-side field on PlayerCombatState, and RunState holds only hp/max_hp -- so the Unblockable flag has nothing to skip and the two produce the same HP loss. (b) HOOKS: CreatureCmd.Damage dispatches Hook.ModifyHpLost over the run state, and lose_hp runs `relic.modify_run_hp_loss(self, loss)` over run.relics (run.py:299-302), which relics/base.py:222-228 documents as exactly that mapping -- so Tungsten Rod's -1 applies on both sides. Also matching: the loss can kill (`self.hp -= ...` with no floor, and RunState.is_dead is `hp <= 0`), which the source likewise allows. EXECUTED (b12-cutters): hp 80 -> 64, i.e. the full 16 with no relic modifiers present. Ordering matches too: C# removes the cards and THEN damages (PrecariousShears.cs:26-30), and precarious_shears.py:18-20 does the same -- which matters because CardSelectCmd's `IsDead` bail (guard N3 of precise_scissors) would suppress the removal if the damage came first. NOTE per binding rule 7: run.py, player.py and relics/base.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `CardsVar(2)` and `DamageVar(16m, ValueProp.Unpowered)` (PrecariousShears.cs:18-22) vs CARDS = 2 and DAMAGE = 16 (precarious_shears.py:14-15)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 2 and 16 are the pinned non-ascension values, and both are read as `.IntValue` / the DamageVar itself at their single call sites (PrecariousShears.cs:26, 30). Re-read against the C# rather than trusted from the port's docstring ('remove 2 chosen cards; take 16 damage') per PROMPT.md bug class 19; both agree. Confirmed by execution (b12-cutters: deck -2, hp -16).

guards.what: N3: the candidate filter and the auto-select semantics
guards.rationale: Identical to relic/precise_scissors N1 and N2 and matched per binding rule 3: FromDeckForRemoval filters on CardModel.IsRemovable = `!Keywords.Contains(Eternal)` (src/Core/Models/CardModel.cs:737) and run.removable_cards() is `not c.eternal` (run.py:360-362); the single-argument CardSelectorPrefs makes MinSelect == MaxSelect == 2 so a deck with two or fewer removable cards is auto-taken, and RunState.select_cards clamps to min(count, len(candidates)) (run.py:371-390). One consequence worth naming for THIS relic: if the deck holds fewer than two removable cards the game still deals the 16 damage, and so does the sim, because the damage is unconditional on both sides. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardSelectCmd.cs, CardModel.cs, run.py and precise_scissors.json are not hashed here.
